title: Sign in to a web app

story.title: The app sent you to sign in
story.what: The app generated a PKCE code_verifier, kept it, and redirected you to the identity provider with its hash (code_challenge).
story.why: The app never sees your password. Only the identity provider authenticates you.
story.matters: PKCE binds the eventual code to this app instance, so an intercepted code is useless.

story.title: You signed in at the identity provider
story.what: You entered credentials (and MFA, if required) on the identity provider's page.
story.why: Authentication happens in one trusted place, under its sign-on policy.
story.matters: Every app gets the same strong sign-in without handling secrets itself.

story.title: The app redeemed the code
story.what: The app sent the code plus the original code_verifier to the token endpoint.
story.why: The identity provider checks the verifier against the challenge from step one.
story.matters: Only the app that started the flow can finish it.

story.title: The app called the API with your token
story.what: The API validated the access token and returned your profile.
story.why: The token says who you are, which app asked, and what it may do.
story.matters: The API trusts the identity provider's signature, not the app's say-so.

subtitle: OpenID Connect authorization code flow with PKCE

outcome.detail: The user authenticated at the identity provider and the app received tokens bound to this sign-in.
outcome.caption: code + verifier redeemed · tokens issued · API returned 200

tokens.label: ID token
tokens.note: The ID token is for the app: proof of who signed in.

tokens.label: Access token
tokens.note: The access token is for the API: what the app may do on the user's behalf.
